### Law_ContainsCenter

[stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato, line 79](../../../../../stdlib/tests/foundation.laws.plato#L79)

```plato
// Same property, stated over AngleInterval's OWN surface.
//
// DOMAIN: AngleInterval reinterprets both Contains and Center as ARC operations
// (intervals.library.plato), so the generic law above does
// not describe this type. Worse, monomorphizing it produces a CHIMERA: the
// interface's linear Center is inlined into the law body (resolution happens
// against IInterval, where the specialization is invisible), while the
// Contains call survives as a call and is re-bound by C# extension-method
// overload resolution to the type's wrap-aware one (tracked as plato-374). Arc
// Contains of a linear midpoint holds for neither reading, and it fails for
// every interval whose stored End - Start exceeds a turn. Restated here on the
// arc surface, where
// the midpoint is Start + Span/2 and containment always holds.
Law_ContainsCenter(self: AngleInterval): Boolean
    => self.Contains(self.Center);
```

    // Even-odd containment. A half-plane sweep would exploit convexity, but the
    // even-odd test is already exact for a simple ring and needs no winding
    // assumption.
    Contains(p: ConvexPolygon2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => p.Points.PolygonContainsPoint(point);
```

    // Inside the boundary and outside every hole.
    Contains(r: PolygonWithHoles2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
        => r.Boundary.Contains(point) && r.Holes.Any(h => h.Contains(point)).Not;
```

### Line 412

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato, line 412](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato#L412).

```plato

    // True when the query's sweep parameter lies in [0, 1] AND the query slid back
    // along Offset onto the base plane lands inside the base ring.
    Contains(p: Prism3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var normal = p.Base.Points.VectorArea.Normalize;
        var origin = p.Base.Points.First;
        var s = origin.Between(point).Dot(normal) / p.Offset.Dot(normal);
        return s >= 0.0 && s <= 1.0
            && p.Base.Points.PlanarPolygonContains(normal, point - p.Offset * s);
    }
```

### Line 458

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato, line 458](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/polygons.library.plato#L458).

```plato

    // True when the query lies between the Apex plane-height and the base
    // (parameter t in [0, 1], t = 0 at the Apex, t = 1 in the base plane) AND the
    // ray from the Apex through the query meets the base plane inside the base
    // ring. Boundary inclusive on t.
    Contains(y: Pyramid3D, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var normal = y.Base.Points.VectorArea.Normalize;
        var origin = y.Base.Points.First;
        var t = 1.0 - origin.Between(point).Dot(normal)
            / origin.Between(y.Apex).Dot(normal);
        return t >= 0.0 && t <= 1.0
            && (t <= 0.0 || y.Base.Points.PlanarPolygonContains(normal,
                y.Apex + y.Apex.Between(point) * (1.0 / t)));
    }
```
